role: Wife of Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA)
summary: Fatima al-Zahra (RA) was the daughter of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and Khadijah bint Khuwaylid (RA), wife of Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA), and mother of Hasan and Husayn (RA). She is regarded in classical Sunni scholarship as the greatest of women in this ummah and among the greatest women of all time. She was deeply devoted to worship, endured poverty with patience, and died approximately six months after the Prophet ﷺ, being buried in Madinah.
biography:
Fatima bint Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hashimiyyah al-Qurashiyyah was born in Makkah, with classical scholars debating whether she was born before or after the beginning of prophethood. The majority position, recorded by Ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat al-Kubra (Vol. 8) and supported by al-Dhahabi in Siyar A'lam al-Nubala' (Vol. 2), places her birth approximately five years before prophethood — around 605 CE. She was the youngest of the Prophet's daughters and the one of his children who survived longest after him.

Fatima grew up in the household of the Prophet ﷺ and Khadijah (RA) and witnessed from childhood the persecution of the early Muslim community. After the death of her mother Khadijah in the Year of Grief (approximately 619 CE), Fatima took on a role of profound emotional and practical support for her father. The bond between father and daughter was extraordinary and remarked upon by many companions. Aisha (RA) narrated: 'I have not seen anyone who resembles the Prophet ﷺ more in his way of speaking and sitting than Fatima. When she came to visit him, he would stand up to greet her, kiss her, and seat her in his place — and when he visited her, she would do the same.' (Sunan Abi Dawud, Kitab al-Adab; al-Dhahabi, Siyar, Vol. 2)

Fatima made the Hijrah to Madinah with the rest of the Prophet's household. In approximately 2 AH, the Prophet ﷺ gave her in marriage to Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA), his cousin, with a modest mahr (dowry) of a shield or some iron armor according to the narrations preserved in Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab al-Nikah). Their household was one of striking simplicity — they ground their own grain, hauled their own water, and lived without servants until the Prophet ﷺ eventually taught them the tasbih that became the famous 'Tasbih Fatima' (SubhanAllah 33 times, Alhamdulillah 33 times, Allahu Akbar 34 times before sleep) as a substitute for domestic help they could not afford. This narration is authenticated in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim.

Fatima bore Ali (RA) four children who survived to adulthood: Hasan, Husayn, Zaynab, and Umm Kulthum. The Prophet ﷺ expressed great love for his grandsons through Fatima, calling Hasan and Husayn 'the leaders of the youth of Paradise' (al-Tirmidhi, Sunan, Kitab al-Manaqib — graded hasan) and wrapping them in his cloak along with Ali and Fatima in the event classical scholars refer to as the Event of the Cloak (hadith al-kisa'), the textual basis for which is in Sahih Muslim (Kitab Fada'il al-Sahaba, narrated by Aisha RA).

The Prophet ﷺ praised Fatima in terms that have no parallel for any other woman in the hadith corpus. He said: 'Fatima is a part of me. Whatever harms her harms me, and whatever pleases her pleases me.' (Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab Fada'il al-Sahaba). He also declared: 'The best women of Paradise are Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, Fatima bint Muhammad, Maryam bint Imran, and Asiyah the wife of Pharaoh.' (Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Musnad — authenticated). Al-Dhahabi records that the Prophet told Fatima directly: 'Are you not pleased to be the Sayyidah (Leader) of the women of the believers, or the Sayyidah of the women of this ummah?' (Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Manaqib).

Fatima's life was one of worship and poverty borne with patience. Al-Dhahabi notes that despite her noble lineage, she worked physically at home without complaint, manifesting the prophetic model of dignity in simplicity. She was deeply devoted to prayer, and companions who visited her home frequently found her in salah.

The Prophet ﷺ died in 11 AH (632 CE) in the month of Rabi' al-Awwal. Fatima was devastated. She is reported to have said after his death: 'How could anyone scatter dust upon you, O Messenger of Allah?' Her grief was apparent to all the companions. She died approximately six months after her father — some narrations say five to six months, others say six months — making her the first of his children to follow him. She was buried in Madinah, though the precise location of her grave is the subject of scholarly discussion and is not definitively established, which is why multiple sites in Madinah have been associated with her burial. Al-Dhahabi, Ibn Sa'd, and Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani all record her death in 11 AH and her burial in Madinah without specifying a location with certainty.

Fatima (RA) holds a uniquely high station in classical Sunni scholarship: she is regarded as the greatest woman of this ummah, and among the four greatest women of all creation along with Khadijah, Maryam, and Asiyah. The Sunni scholarly tradition honors her with deep reverence as Ahl al-Bayt, without the doctrinal accretions associated with later Shia theological development. She is remembered for her worship, her patience, her grief at her father's death, and her role as the mother of the Prophet's surviving male line.
